issues.text: Slightly overstated: Docker also calls anonymous volumes volumes (volumes.md: anonymous volumes "persist even if you remove the container that uses them"), so 'the word volume' is not reserved for the named kind. The point being made (bind mounts are not volumes) is correct; anonymous volumes are out of scope, so this only needs a narrower wording.
issues.quote: Docker keeps the word volume for the named kind: a bind mount is a separate type
issues.fix: Replace with: "Docker does not call a bind mount a volume: it is a separate type" (rest of the sentence unchanged).

issues.text: Still open from round 1 (wording kept from the outline): from what I know about the garbage collector, removing a variable does not delete the object it pointed to, so the comparison argues against the misconception as much as for it. The correction itself is clear.
issues.quote: the same way removing a variable deletes what it pointed to
issues.fix: Only if the outline owner agrees: change the comparison to 'the same way removing a container deletes its own changes'. Otherwise leave as is.

issues.text: Summary line 4 says the scripts run 'only on the very first start', but the second misconception and quiz q4 say they run again when the volume is removed and the data folder is empty. The two statements pulled against each other for a moment.
issues.quote: `schema.sql` and `seed.sql` run only when that data folder is empty, which is only on the very first start.
issues.fix: Replace 'which is only on the very first start' with 'such as on the very first start or after the volume is removed'.

issues.text: q4, explanation d: the last clause 'only the empty data folder did' does not attach to anything ('did' what?). I had to re-read it to get that it means the empty data folder is what made the scripts run.
issues.quote: but whether the API runs has nothing to do with them; only the empty data folder did.
issues.fix: End the sentence with '; what made them run was the empty data folder.'

issues.text: q4, correct explanation: 'the scripts ran, adding the product and losing every order' reads as if running the scripts deleted the orders. The lesson says the orders were lost because the volume was removed.
issues.quote: Removing the volume emptied the data folder: the scripts ran, adding the product and losing every order.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: 'Removing the volume deleted every order and emptied the data folder, so the scripts ran and added the product.'

issues.text: q2: the correct option is the longest and nearly repeats the first misconception's correction ('the next `db` container picks up the same data'), so I can match it by wording.
issues.quote: False, because the named volume stays and the next `db` container finds the same data.
